proposed_Babylonian_or_Persian_equivalen: Balāṭ-šarri-uṣur "Protect the life of the king!"
attested?: NO: the name is not attested; names of the same type are
attestations_(corpus, text, line, date,: Not found among Prosobab's 3,545 names / 21,028 individuals, nor in the ORACC proper-name glossaries of RIBo, HBTIN, BabCity, Borsippa, ARIo or SAAo (cumulative). Names of the same type that ARE attested: Balāssu-uṣur "Protect his life!" (patronym; ba-laṭ-su-ÙRU; UET 4, 27, Ur, Damqia archive, 11.XIII.8 of an unnamed king); [...]-balāssu(?)-uṣur ([...]-TIN-su-PAB; VAT 3155 = San Nicolò–Ungnad no. 251, 2+.IV.1 Cyrus = 538 BCE); Nabû-balāṭu-uṣur (dAG-ba-la-ṭu-ÙRU; BM 25841, 30.V.27 Darius I = 495 BCE); Bān-šarri-uṣur "Protect the creator of the king!" (ba-ni-LUGAL-ÙRU; BM 30446 = Abraham 2004 no. 12, 4.VIII.24 Darius I = 498 BCE); Abat-šarri-uṣur "Protect the word of the king" (SAAo, Neo-Assyrian, {1}a-bat-LUGAL-PAB); Itti-šarri-balāṭu (KI-LUGAL-TIN; BM 30509 = Wunsch 1993b no. 193, Nbn 11); Bēl-šarru-bulliṭ (dEN-LUGAL-bul-liṭ; BM 64235, Darius I 11). Possible alternative containing a divine title: Bēlet-šarru-uṣur "O Lady, protect the king" (dGAŠAN-LUGAL-ÙRU; BM 26736, unpublished, Til-būri, Atkuppu archive, 28.III.24 Darius I = 498 BCE; Prosobab iid 29777).
assessment: Balāṭ-šarri-uṣur would be a well-formed name of an attested type, but it is unattested in the data examined. It does NOT contain Bēl (balāṭ = "life"). The Hebrew spelling DOES separate the two names: בלטשאצר b-l-ṭ-š-ʾ-ṣ-r vs בלשאצר b-l-š-ʾ-ṣ-r (5:1-29) / בלאשצר (5:30; 7:1; 8:1). Its ṭ (emphatic) fits Akk. balāṭ; Bēl/Bēlet have no ṭ (Bēlet has plain t). Both Hebrew names end in -šʾṣr with no r written for šarru; in Belshazzar this ending must stand for -šarra-uṣur, so blṭšʾṣr is consistent with Balāṭ-šar(ri)-uṣur. My own observation, not from a source: it is equally consistent with the attested Balāssu-uṣur (= balāṭ-šu-uṣur). The gloss in 4:5 ("after the name of my god") links the name to Bēl, but its consonants do not contain Bēl unless ṭ is ignored.
unverified_or_not_checked: How Aramaic scribes rendered Akk. t/ṭ in Bēlet; any other attestation of Balāṭ-šarri-uṣur outside Prosobab/ORACC (e.g. CAD, PNA, NB archives not in Prosobab) was not checked

attestations_(corpus, text, line, date,: RIBo Nabonidus 32 (Schaudig AOAT 256 no. 2.2; Ur cylinders BM 91125-91128 etc.) ii 23: u₃ ša₂ {m}{d}EN-LUGAL-URU₃ DUMU reš-tu-u₂ ṣi-it lib₃-bi-ia ("and as for Bēl-šarra-uṣur, the eldest son, my offspring"). RIBo Nabonidus 27 (Schaudig no. 2.14; RIBo provenience: Ur) i 35, ii 24, iii 22, iii 76, same formula. Prosobab (title mār šarri): 9 archival attestations from Nbn 1 (555/4) to Nbn 12 (544/3), all spelled {m}{d}EN-LUGAL-ÙRU; see part2_belshazzar_attestations.csv. The name was also borne by private persons: son of Balāṭu (BM 31260, BM 31080; Nbn 1); son of Nabû-šumu-iddin (VAT 3028; 42 Nbk II = 563/2); son of Nūrea (BM 77873 = Nbn 111; Nbn 3); Neo-Assyrian Bel-šarru-uṣur (SAAo, 24 instances, {1}EN-MAN-PAB).
assessment: A standard Babylonian name of the DN-šarru-uṣur type (Prosobab lists more than 25 DN-šarru-uṣur names). Belshazzar is securely attested as crown prince in royal inscriptions and contracts. RIBo normalizes the name as Bel-šarra-uṣur, Prosobab as Bēl-šarru-uṣur. In the data he carries only the title mār šarri; no title šarru was found for him.
unverified_or_not_checked: Chronicle and other literary sources (Nabonidus Chronicle, Verse Account) are not in the downloaded data

attestations_(corpus, text, line, date,: RIBo (babylon7) spellings: syllabic {d}na-bi-um-ku-du-ur₂-ri-u₂-ṣu-ur₂ (38 tokens; e.g. Nebuchadnezzar II 012-016 i 1), {d}AG-ku-dur₂-ri-u₂-ṣu-ur₂ (11; e.g. Nebuchadnezzar II 002 i 1, 003 l.1), {d}AG-ku-dur₂-ri-URU₃ (7); logographic {d}AG-NIG₂.DU-URU₃ (16), {m}{d}AG-NIG₂.GUB-URU₃ (12), {d}MUATI-NIG₂.DU-URU₃ (5) and others. Prosobab gives kudurru the meaning "heir".
assessment: The Akkadian form has r (kudurri). The syllabic writings confirm it, so the Jeremiah/Ezekiel form with r (נבוכדראצר) is the closer one. The Daniel/Kings/Esther form has n in the place of the first r. That this n comes from dissimilation is a standard explanation, not verified here.

attestations_(corpus, text, line, date,: SAAo lemma ša-rēši "eunuch" (Neo-Assyrian 255, Neo-Babylonian 82 instances), including rab forms: {LU₂}GAL-SAG (NA); GAL-{LU₂}SAG and {LU₂}GAL-SAG (NB letters). Borsippa/BabCity {lu₂}SAG = ša rēši. Prosobab: qallu ša rab ša rēši "slave of the chief courtier" (BM 77907 = Bertin 1017-1018, Babylon, 15.I.1 Šamaš-šumu-ukīn = 667 BCE); ša rēš šarri (28 individuals) and rēš šarri (20).
assessment: A good match. The title is current in Neo-Assyrian, Neo-Babylonian and Achaemenid Babylonia, and Hebrew applies rab-sārîs to Babylonian officials elsewhere (Jer 39). That sārîs derives from ša rēši is standard (not re-derived here).

proposed_Babylonian_or_Persian_equivalen: Akk. Kaldu (land), Kaldāya (people); "kaldû" as a diviner?
attestations_(corpus, text, line, date,: SAAo: Kaldaya "Chaldean" (EN, 31 instances) and Kaldu "Chaldea" (GN, 19) are always ethnic or geographic. Examples: SAA 8 316 r 1 "ina rabûti ša Kaldu lū Aramu" ("among the magnates of Chaldea or Aram", in a substitute-king context; the rab āšipi in o 18 is a separate person); SAA 10 347 r 15' and 351 b.e. 23-24 (omen apodoses listing lands: Hatti, Kaldu, Sutu, Aribi); SAA 10 353 r 16 bēt Kaldani. There is no Kaldu/Kaldaya in the RIBo Neo-Babylonian dynasty inscriptions (232 texts), HBTIN (487), BabCity, Borsippa, or the ADSD astronomical diaries glossary (401 texts). Kaldû is not among Prosobab's 400 titles.
assessment: In the cuneiform data examined, Kaldu/Kaldāya never denotes a class of diviners; it is always the people or land of Chaldea. Daniel's professional sense has no support in these texts. Daniel 5:30 itself uses the ethnic sense.
unverified_or_not_checked: Greek and Hellenistic usage of "Chaldaioi" for astrologers (not checked); Late Babylonian scholarly texts outside these projects (e.g. CAMS/GKAB colophons) were not searched for this
